chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'What do you say regarding bartering wheat with sawiq (mash of wheat and barley)?' He said, 'Similar with similar, there is no problem with it.' I said, 'Suppose he has a yield (extra quality/quantity) or has an excess?' He said, 'Does he not have maintenance (cost/effort) for it?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'This by this.' And he said, 'When the two things are different, there is no problem with two with one, hand to hand.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for permissible barter of foodstuffs in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that exchanging similar foodstuffs like wheat for sawiq is permissible with slight variations in quality or quantity, justified by the 'ma'unah' (maintenance or processing effort) involved. For dissimilar items, the hadith emphasizes the 'hand-to-hand' (yadan bi-yad) requirement for immediate exchange, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence distinguishing between riba al-fadl and riba al-nasi'ah. This ruling reflects the practical economic realities of the time, ensuring fairness while allowing for minor discrepancies in value when the items are of the same genus.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said to himasws, ‘What are youasws saying regarding the (bartering of) the wheat with the Saweyq (mash of wheat and barley). So heasws said: ‘Similar with similar, there is no problem with it’. I said, ‘(Supposing) he happens to have a yield for him or happens to have excess for him?’ So heasws said: ‘Does he not have maintenance for it?’ I said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘This by this’. And heasws said: ‘When the two things are different, so there is no problem with two with one, hand to hand’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about his opinion on wheat and the sawiq (mush made of wheat or barley). He (the Imam) said, ‘Their exchange in equal measures is not harmful.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if one has a certain yield or preference over the other?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Does it not have expenses and maintenance?’ I replied, ‘Yes, it has such overheads.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This is for that.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘If they are two different things then exchange of one for two at the same time is permissible.’”
